blocks.orig: It’s official: Tanzania is Africa’s Leading Destination 2025, for the second year in a row and third time overall. Tanzania truly made history, winning 27 out of the 60 awards presented in Dar es Salaam on 28 June 2025. Besides hotels and various tourism companies, the government side won awards for this year’s Best Tourist Attractions, Best Safari Destination in Africa and Best Airport in Africa. This is even more impressive bearing in mind that only one year prior, Tanzania “only” won five awards.
blocks.html: Now it’s official: for the second year running and the third time in total, Tanzania has been named Africa’s Leading Destination 2025. The country made history at the ceremony in Dar es Salaam on 28 June 2025, taking home 27 of the 60 awards on offer. Alongside hotels and a range of tourism companies, the government side collected prizes for this year’s Best Tourist Attractions, Best Safari Destination in Africa and Best Airport in Africa. That is all the more impressive when you consider that just a year earlier, Tanzania won “only” five awards.

blocks.orig: Tanzania’s President Samia Suluhu Hassan left nothing to chance, putting the focus on driving tourism in Tanzania through numerous initiatives: the Royal Tour documentary promoted the country’s attractions internationally, increased budget allocations opened doors for the tourism sector as well as for investors and improved infrastructure made conservation areas more accessible.
blocks.html: Tanzania’s President Samia Suluhu Hassan left nothing to chance and made boosting tourism in Tanzania a priority through a number of initiatives: the Royal Tour documentary showcased the country’s attractions to an international audience, larger budget allocations created opportunities for both the tourism sector and investors, and better infrastructure made the conservation areas easier to reach.

blocks.orig: Reading all this, it doesn’t come as a surprise that the Tanzania Tourist Board also won Africa’s Leading Tourist Board 2025.
blocks.html: With all that in mind, it is hardly surprising that the Tanzania Tourist Board was also crowned Africa’s Leading Tourist Board 2025.

blocks.orig: Since 1993 the World Travel Awards have been recognizing excellence in tourism and hospitality worldwide. On 28 June 2025 the World Travel Awards Africa and Indian Ocean Gala Ceremony was held in Dar es Salaam for the first time, which makes these victories even more special to Tanzania.
blocks.html: The World Travel Awards have honoured excellence in tourism and hospitality around the world since 1993. For the first time, the World Travel Awards Africa and Indian Ocean Gala Ceremony took place in Dar es Salaam on 28 June 2025, which makes these wins all the more special for Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Not only do the awards acknowledge outstanding performance in the travel and tourism industry, they also play an essential part in increasing destination visibility, competitiveness and investments.
blocks.html: The awards do more than recognise outstanding work in the travel and tourism industry; they also play a key role in raising a destination’s visibility, competitiveness and investment.

blocks.orig: Of course, we cannot list each and every award Tanzania has won (and yes, we are proud that the country won so many), but let’s have a look at the highlights, shall we?
blocks.html: Naturally, we can’t go through every single award Tanzania collected (and yes, we are proud the country won so many), but shall we take a look at the highlights?

blocks.orig: Tanzania is home to 22 national parks, and seven of them won awards at the WTA 2025, with the Serengeti National Park coming first twice: once as Africa’s Leading Big 5 National Park 2025 and once as Africa’s Leading National Park 2025. Despite these two achievements and being one of the most famous national parks in the world (rightly so!), Africa’s Leading Tourist Attraction 2025 is the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Here, you can not only be wowed by unique landscapes, but also by the highest wildlife density in the country.
blocks.html: Of Tanzania’s 22 national parks, seven received awards at the WTA 2025, and the Serengeti National Park took first place twice: as Africa’s Leading Big 5 National Park 2025 and as Africa’s Leading National Park 2025. Even with these two wins, and its status as one of the world’s most famous national parks (and rightly so!), the title of Africa’s Leading Tourist Attraction 2025 went to the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. There, unique landscapes will amaze you, and so will the highest density of wildlife in the country.

blocks.orig: On top of all that, the Kilimanjaro National Park took the pole (pole) position as Africa’s Leading Mountain National Park. If you want to stand on the roof of Africa yourself or explore these beauties straight away, we can understand. But where to stay? How about award-winning lodges?
blocks.html: And to top it all off, Kilimanjaro National Park claimed pole (pole) position as Africa’s Leading Mountain National Park. We understand if you now want to reach the roof of Africa yourself or set off to explore these gems right away. So where should you stay? Why not at an award-winning lodge?

blocks.orig: The Chem Chem Lodge can be found close to Lake Manyara and has perfected the art of “Slow Safari”. Here, time seems to pass a little slower than everywhere else. In the eight tented suites you can rest after having explored the country with the Maasai on foot or marvelling at the diverse wildlife on the 20,000 hectares connecting Tarangire and Lake Manyara National Parks, managed by Chem Chem. No wonder it was crowned Tanzania’s Leading Luxury Safari Lodge 2025.
blocks.html: Close to Lake Manyara you will find Chem Chem Lodge, which has mastered the art of “Slow Safari”. Time here seems to move a little more slowly than anywhere else. The eight tented suites are the place to unwind after exploring the area on foot with the Maasai, or after admiring the varied wildlife across the 20,000 hectares managed by Chem Chem that link Tarangire and Lake Manyara National Parks. Small wonder it was named Tanzania’s Leading Luxury Safari Lodge 2025.

blocks.orig: Tanzania’s Leading Hotel 2025, the Gran Meliá Arusha, is located in the city of Arusha, spoiling guests with breathtaking views on the spectacular Mount Meru. With a spa, two pools, cosy rooms and several restaurants, this luxury hotel leaves no wish unfulfilled. Explore the city itself, head out on a safari in Arusha National Park, and end your day with high-class cuisine and a sundowner while watching the sun go down.
blocks.html: Named Tanzania’s Leading Hotel 2025, the Gran Meliá Arusha sits in the city of Arusha and treats its guests to breathtaking views of the spectacular Mount Meru. A spa, two pools, cosy rooms and several restaurants mean this luxury hotel leaves nothing to be desired. Discover the city, go on safari in Arusha National Park, then round off the day with fine dining and a sundowner as the sun sets.

blocks.orig: This unique hotel scored twice at the WTA, winning also the prize for Tanzania’s Leading Hotel Suite 2025. A king-sized bed, mountain view and 164qm2: uniting traditional luxury with African hospitality, this suite is truly one-of-a-kind. Next to amenities of the highest class, you also enjoy the hotel’s RedLevel VIP service for a perfect experience from A to Z.
blocks.html: This distinctive hotel won twice at the WTA, also taking the title of Tanzania’s Leading Hotel Suite 2025. With a king-sized bed, a view of the mountain and 164qm2, the suite brings together traditional luxury and African hospitality in a way that is genuinely one-of-a-kind. As well as top-class amenities, you benefit from the hotel’s RedLevel VIP service, so everything is taken care of from A to Z.

blocks.orig: The dreamy island of Zanzibar was also victorious at the World Travel Awards 2025, claiming top spots for both Africa’s Leading Festival & Event Destination and Africa’s Leading Beach Destination. With its endless stretches of white sandy beaches and the glistening Indian Ocean on one side and postcard-perfect palm trees on the other, this accolade is more than deserved!
blocks.html: The dreamy island of Zanzibar also came out on top at the World Travel Awards 2025, winning first place as both Africa’s Leading Festival & Event Destination and Africa’s Leading Beach Destination. Given its endless white sandy beaches, with the sparkling Indian Ocean on one side and picture-postcard palm trees on the other, the recognition is more than deserved!

blocks.orig: The (official) perfect place to experience these pristine beaches, is the Tulia Zanzibar Unique Beach Resort, which won the award for Zanzibar’s Leading Boutique Resort 2025. The spacious accommodation is located on the northeast of Zanzibar and welcomes you with a huge garden along the beach, only sixteen villas and a wonderful feeling of peace. Experiencing the best beaches in Africa in the best boutique hotel in Africa – what more can you wish for?
blocks.html: If you want the (official) perfect spot to enjoy these unspoilt beaches, look to the Tulia Zanzibar Unique Beach Resort, winner of Zanzibar’s Leading Boutique Resort 2025. Set on the northeast of Zanzibar, the spacious resort greets you with a vast garden along the beach, just sixteen villas and a lovely sense of calm. The best beaches in Africa combined with the best boutique hotel in Africa – what more could you ask for?

blocks.orig: Winning these many awards at the WTA shows that Tanzania has become a tourism powerhouse in Africa and worldwide, committing to further develop sustainable tourism which benefits nature, people and the country.
blocks.html: Taking home so many awards at the WTA shows that Tanzania has grown into a tourism powerhouse, both in Africa and globally, and that it is committed to developing sustainable tourism further, to the benefit of nature, people and the country.
